thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Dip, Putting S&P 500 On Pace For 3rd Down Session In A Row

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Dip, Putting S&P 500 On Pace For 3rd Down Session In A Row
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch
Caterpillar's earnings are on the docket before the open
U.S. stock futures pointed to a small decline at the open Monday, setting the S&P 500 on course for a third losing session in a row, a sign the market is still absorbing the recent bruising from some disappointing earnings.
The broad benchmark's strong month is shaping up to end on a downbeat note, with buying appetite waning on that second-quarter earnings gloom.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures slipped by 17 points, or 0.1%, to 25,397, while S&P 500 futures shed 3.50 points, or 0.1%, to 2,814. Nasdaq-100 futures dipped by 7.25 points, or 0.1%, to 7,294.
On Friday, the Dow , S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite closed lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-tech-stocks-hint-at-rebound-ahead-of-gdp-twitter-results-2018-07-27), with the Dow snapping a three-day winning streak, while the S&P and Nasdaq both fell for a second-straight session.
With two days left in July, the three gauges are showing healthy gains for the month. The S&P is up 3.7% for the month to date, representing its largest such rise since January, while the Dow and Nasdaq are higher by 4.9% and 3%, respectively.
What's driving markets?
Investors have been shaking off some worries about global trade tensions this month, instead focusing on upbeat readings on second-quarter earnings.
But some internet companies tumbled last week after disappointing releases and weighed on the broad market, including Facebook Inc (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-stock-crushed-after-revenue-user-growth-miss-2018-07-25). and Twitter Inc (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/twitter-user-numbers-slip-as-it-purges-fake-accounts-2018-07-27-7103732). Apple Inc.'s report late Tuesday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-most-boring-quarter-of-the-year-still-holds-some-intrigue-2018-07-27) will be key this week.
Check out:Earnings Watch -- Even Apple takes a back seat to Elon Musk right now (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/earnings-watch-even-apple-takes-a-back-seat-to-elon-musk-right-now-2018-07-29)
What are strategists saying?
"The high contribution that FANG stocks have had toward the S&P's return has been referenced as a market warning, as if their strength is masking weakness underneath the S&P's surface," said Ari Wald,
"In fact, 92% of the S&P's 2018 gain has occurred outside the Big 6 (AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, FB, GOOG, NFLX) on an equal-weighted basis -- showing there's been broad opportunities to make money this year," Wald added, referring to Apple Inc.(AAPL) , Microsoft Corp.(MSFT) , Amazon.com Inc.(AMZN) , Facebook Inc.(FB) , Google parent Alphabet Inc.(GOOGL)(GOOGL)and Netflix Inc.(NFLX)
Which stocks are in focus?
CBS Corp.'s stock (CBSA)could face more selling after falling 6.1% Friday on news that the media company's board would investigate allegations of personal misconduct (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cbs-board-to-investigate-allegations-of-misconduct-by-ceo-leslie-moonves-2018-07-27-1510354) by CEO Les Moonves. Some board members discussed over the weekend whether Moonves should step aside (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cbs-board-mulls-whether-ceo-leslie-moonves-should-step-aside-2018-07-29), after a New Yorker article late Friday reported that six women have come forward saying he sexually harassed them over a period spanning three decades.
MGM Resorts International's (MGM) stock could be active after the casino operator said it will create a U.S. sports betting and online gaming joint venture (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gvc-mgm-resorts-to-create-us-sports-betting-jv-2018-07-30) with U.K. gambling company GVC Holdings PLC (GVC.LN) . The alliance is seen as taking advantage of the opportunities opened up by the recent U.S. Supreme Court ruling on sports betting.
Shares in heavy machinery maker Caterpillar Inc.(CAT)and mall owner Simon Property Group Inc.(SPG)are likely to see active trading as they're among the companies expected to post earnings before the open.
What are other markets doing?
European stocks were trading lower, while Asian markets closed with losses (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-markets-across-asia-slip-led-by-hong-kong-2018-07-29).
Oil futures were gaining, as gold futures and the ICE U.S. Dollar Index dipped.
Which economic reports are getting attention?
A June report on pending home sales is slated to hit at 10 a.m. Eastern Time.
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
On the Federal Reserve front, the central bank's policy committee is slated to begin a two-day meeting on Tuesday. Economists expect it won't raise interest rates, but see it issuing a statement Wednesday making it clear that more rate hikes are coming (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fed-to-send-clear-message-that-more-rate-hikes-are-coming-2018-07-27). Two more rate hikes this year have been signaled, but the first isn't expected until September.
Other central banks are holding meetings this week: The Bank of Japan is seen as holding broadly to its current monetary policy at its July 30-31 meeting, while the Bank of England is expected to lift interest rates on Thursday in only its second hike in a decade.
